newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire's Kabila says no rebel ceasefire in war.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Kabila says no rebel ceasefire in war.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Wednesday spurned calls for a ceasefire and said there would be no let-up in his offensive to remove President Mobutu Sese Seko.

Kabila, head of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), told Reuters by telephone from Zaire's second largest city Lubumbashi that the "people are against a ceasefire".

Kabila was responding to remarks by U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan who on Tuesday appealed to U.N. members to press Kabila to seek a negotiated solution through a ceasefire and sustained talks on the country's future.
"How can I declare a ceasefire when the people are against one? The people do not want a ceasefire, they want an end to this corrupt regime," Kabila said.
Kabila, who arrived in Lubumbashi on Monday, said he would address a rally on Thursday and would meet South African President Nelson Mandela "very, very soon" to discuss the Zaire conflict.

South Africa on Tuesday predicted dramatic progress within days in ending the civil war to avert mayhem in Kinshasa, a city of over five million people which is the last remaining stronghold of Mobutu.

But after two days of anti-Mobutu protests which brought the Zairean capital to a standstill, many residents are asking what happens if the rebels reach town. Concern is growing over the prospect of bloodshed and anarchy in Zaire's sprawling capital, diplomats say.
The United States, France, Belgium and Britain have stationed more than 1,000 military personnel in the nearby Congolese capital Brazzaville.
